caption: The number of distinct letter arrangements of MISSISSIPPI: 1 M, 4 I's, 4 S's, 2 P's
The coefficient of $a^2 b^3 c$ in $(a+b+c)^6$
With two arguments it reduces to [[Binomial]]: $\binom{n_1+n_2}{n_1}$
Orderless: permuting the arguments doesn't change the value
All-ones parts give $n!$: every part is a single labelled item
All-zero arguments still give the empty product, 1
A single argument is always 1: there's only one way to split n items into one group
A single symbolic argument is also 1
With no arguments it is the empty product, 1
sage.note: Sage raises IndexError: tuple index out of range; ours answers 1.

A single argument n is binomial(n, n), which compute-engine and Wolfram extend to a negative n as 1 (binom(-2, -2) = 1, see the Binomial rows); Sage follows the combinatorial C(n, k) = 0 convention outside 0 <= k <= n and gives 0.
julia.note: A single argument n is binomial(n, n), which compute-engine and Wolfram extend to a negative n as 1 (binom(-2, -2) = 1, see the Binomial rows); Combinatorics.jl follows the combinatorial C(n, k) = 0 convention outside 0 <= k <= n and gives 0.
